chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If you forget a prayer or pray it without ablution, and there are missed prayers upon you, begin with the first of them, call the Adhan for it, and call the Iqamah, then pray it, then pray what follows it with an Iqamah, an Iqamah for each prayer.

He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: And if you have prayed Dhuhr and the morning prayer (Fajr) has been missed by you, and you remember it, pray it at whatever hour you remember it, even after Asr, and whenever you remember a missed prayer, you pray it.

And he said: If you forget Dhuhr until you pray Asr, and you remember it while you are in prayer or after finishing it, intend it as the first (Dhuhr), then pray Asr, for it is the four rak'ahs that you have prayed in place of the four (of Dhuhr).
And if you remember that you did not pray the first (Dhuhr) while you are in the prayer of Asr, and you have prayed two rak'ahs from it, then pray the remaining two rak'ahs, stand up and pray Asr.
And if you remember that you did not pray Asr until the time of Maghrib entered, and you do not fear missing it (Asr), then pray Asr, then pray Maghrib.
And if you have already prayed Maghrib, stand up and pray Asr.
And if you have prayed two rak'ahs from Maghrib, then you remember Asr, intend Asr, then give Salam, then pray Maghrib.
And if you have prayed the final Isha, and you forgot Maghrib, stand up and pray Maghrib.

And if you remember it (Maghrib) and you have prayed two rak'ahs from the final Isha, or you are standing in the third (rak'ah), intend Maghrib, then give Salam, then stand up and pray the final Isha.
And if you have forgotten the final Isha until you have prayed Fajr, then pray the final Isha.
And if you remember it while you are in one rak'ah or in the second of the morning (Fajr), intend Isha, then stand up and pray the morning (Fajr), call the Adhan and Iqamah.
And if Maghrib and Isha have both been missed by you, begin with them before you pray the morning (Fajr), begin with Maghrib then Isha.
And if you fear that the morning (Fajr) will be missed if you begin with them (Maghrib and Isha), then begin with Maghrib, then with the morning (Fajr), then pray Isha.

And if you fear that the prayer of the morning (Fajr) will be missed if you begin with Maghrib, then pray the morning (Fajr), then pray Maghrib and Isha, begin with the first of them because they are both make-up prayers.
Whichever of them you remember, do not pray them except after the ray of the sun.
He said: I asked: For what reason is that? He said: Because you do not fear missing it.
ai.seo_question: How to make up missed prayers if you forget them or pray without wudu?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, this hadith provides a comprehensive jurisprudential framework for *qada* (make-up) prayers, emphasizing the necessity of performing each missed prayer individually with its own Adhan and Iqamah. It distinguishes between scenarios where one fears missing the current prayer's time versus those where one does not, thereby guiding the faithful on the optimal sequence of *qada* and *hadhr* (current) prayers to ensure both validity and timeliness.
